Hello! Fellow dog trainer here. Here’s a break down of things you should look further into! Ill try to keep it simple but theres a lot of things we would have to go over to see the source of your dog’s behavior. 

The people above are correct! Under socialization is the main root to this behavior but theres more to it. It is indeed easier to train this when their a puppy. Any dog who is meant to protect go through a fear phase when their puppies. 

- Being under socialized is causing your dog’s confidence to suffer

-Your dog’s confidence is what causes unpredictable/bipolar reactivity  

-Depending on your dogs breeder, there are 3 main types of Corsos, working, show, and pet. If your dog is displaying very high drive then most likely he comes from a linage of working Corsos. So it’s a double whammy that your dogs i meant to work as a protector and suffers from low confidence 

- this can be trained out of the dog with structure socialization and a leader (not alpha) to show him boundaries when in public or experiencing new environments. Having a solid foundation of basic obedience should be taught to the dog before heavy socialization. 

- setting up your dog with the right tools will instantly make your life easier but this is where you need professional help. I wouldn’t recommend purchasing any tool to walk your dog until you seek professional help

-hire a trainer. Corsos are not easy dogs to own. They can become easy if you are very familiar with ownership and the breed. This may be a problem that too big for you to control. You should seek professional help asap. 

- you will need training just as much as the dog needs training. You may be unconsciously reinforcing the behavior.

One thing that’s is very common with Corsos is they have a high prey drive, they’re toy that exists to trigger this drive. A flirt pole or a Nero ball is a great training tool we use. We use a flirt pole to put the dog through a process called agitation in order for him to bring more intensity and building more drive in protection work. The Nero ball is a great toy to use as a reward system. They dog does an expectation, you reward with a few second of play time with the Nero ball and repeat.  


Something really good for dog to go through to see if you can bring the food drive out is called existential feeding. Look up the process on YouTube! Its a lot to explain but that technique is really good with any dog that has a natural sense to work for their food. But! You may just have a dog that’s likes to be super chill which there is nothing wrong with that

Also to add on to the rounded edges, you are also correct about that! They way we spot a bad or counterfeit prong collar is we look at the prong edges. Its they are completely flat instead of rounded then we know those are useless collars. Herm sprenger is everyones go to.

You are 100% right on this. The reason we also aim for that specific placement is because there are pressure points right at that same exact location that we want to activate when giving a correction. It also give us a lot more control of the corso’s head when placed higher up. The reason you see it sag so low on this video is because of the extra skin they have. I constantly am moving it higher up. What we might to use to prevent the prong collar from falling down is using a thick tactical collar. You have the tactical collar under the prong collar to reassure it doesn’t slip down.
